page: Microsoft Azure D8ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It includes a 472 GB local storage disk and supports Premium Storage. The CPU architecture is x86_64, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and featuring hardware support for AVX-512 instructions, AES cryptography, and SHA extensions.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 607.6 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak, registering in the bottom 25% at 38.94 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth remains average at 28.76 GB/sec. The server demonstrates average throughput for static web serving at 12.28 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 11.53 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff for the D8ads_v6 is the performance drop in uncached memory read operations and medium-model LLM prompt processing, both of which rank in the bottom 25%. However, its balanced resource allocation and strong single-core capabilities make it suitable for workloads such as general-purpose web serving, software compilation, database operations, and text processing.
